sph_interpretive_translation: Thus, the performance of libation-water rites is enjoined for deceased maternal grandfathers, preceptors, and paternal uncles; similarly, optional libations are prescribed for deceased friends, brothers-in-law, sisters’ husbands, fathers-in-law, and officiating priests.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through relational dharma, not bloodline alone
Causation in ritual duty arises from conscious connection, not biological inheritance
Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond immediate kinship to include chosen affiliations
Restoration logic honors relational integrity even after death
Consciousness alignment requires honoring all beings who shaped one's dharma journey
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person has deceased relations including maternal grandfather, preceptor, paternal uncle, THEN perform mandatory libation-water rites
IF a person has deceased friends, brothers-in-law, sisters' husbands, fathers-in-law, or officiating priests, THEN optional libation-water rites MAY be performed
IF relation contributed to dharmic formation of individual consciousness, THEN ritual obligation EXISTS
IF no physical heir present, THEN designated spiritual successor SHALL execute rite
IF omission occurs due to unawareness, THEN completion process SHALL restore causal field without blame
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving posthumous obligations and familial duties, the Supreme Court shall recognize that dharma-derived responsibilities extend beyond statutory definitions of family. The court shall acknowledge relational hierarchies rooted in consciousness-forming bonds and ensure state policies facilitate ritual completions when legally challenged by those carrying such dharmic lineage.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal continuity between life-shaping relationships and post-death obligations. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential fulfillment of relational debts without punitive framing. Responsibility aligns proportionally with the degree of conscious influence exerted during lifetime. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that neglect results in karmic incompleteness rather than judicial penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Initiate guided ritual performance upon notification of omission
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Assign qualified relative or disciple to carry out rite if primary executor unavailable
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Provide scriptural instruction and priestly guidance to enable correct execution
Integrity Reintegration System: Confirm energetic resolution through certified mantra completion
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority of Sanatana Dharma. This law restores relational dharma, upholds consciousness-based obligation, affirms non-punitive reality, and positions awareness as the ultimate adjudicator of truth.
